title: Pacing and feel: making a recording feel human
text: record_demo() exposes four pacing controls: typing_speed — delay per character. "60ms" default; faster ("40ms") snappier reads urgent, slower ("100ms") reads deliberate. line_pause — sleep line, output renders. Default "500ms". Bump lines whose output want viewer read (summary(), str()); leave short setup lines. paragraph_pause — unset default. set, blank lines expression become sleep duration instead typed empty lines. Use give viewers beat thought units. typing_speed_jitter — number [0, 1]. jitter, per-line typing speed sampled uniformly within ±jitter typing_speed. default 0 means every line types exactly typing_speed; 0.3 means line somewhere 70% 130% base speed. Set set.seed() first want reproducible jitter. compose. recipes show difference makes.

text: five-line demo, recorded three times different pacing.

what: Mechanical: defaults, no jitter, no paragraph beat
title: Pacing and feel: making a recording feel human

title: Pacing and feel: making a recording feel human
text: Dense computational output (model summaries, large data previews): bump line_pause "1s" "1.5s" viewers can actually read . Short snippet (3–4 lines, tight file-size budget): drop typing_speed "40ms" skip jitter — speed wins realism . Walking stepwise tutorial: paragraph_pause = "1.5s" moderate jitter give viewers time anticipate step.

title: Hand-writing tape scripts
text: record_demo() assumes want type R freshly-spawned R REPL. Reach hand-written tape : want record shell session (git, npm, pip, …) rather R code. need multi-shell setup R starts — clearing screen, exporting environment variable, navigating project directory. want fine-grained timing: per-key Backspace corrections, arrow-key navigation, Wait /regex/ synchronisation output. want multiple Screenshot directives single recording flipbook. everything else, record_demo() saves typing.

what: Gotchas vhsR works around for you
title: Hand-writing tape scripts
text: Three corners vhs tape syntax vhsR papers internally; ’ll want copy pattern writing tape hand. Slashes unquoted paths look like Wait regex literal. vhs parses /something/ regex. fails: Quote paths: Strings double quotes inside Type need backtick fallback: vhsR:::quote_for_tape() picks right form per line. Screenshot occasionally racy. vhs takes screenshot moment directive runs tape, headless renderer sometimes hasn’t repainted yet. Leave Sleep 200ms (longer) immediately Screenshot safe.
code: Output /tmp/demo.gif Screenshot /tmp/frame.png Output "/tmp/demo.gif" Screenshot "/tmp/frame.png" Type "x <- \"hello\""    # broken — vhs doesn't handle the escape Type `x <- "hello"`      # works — vhs treats backticks as quotes

title: Hand-writing tape scripts
text: Pass file path: …multi-line string: code paths go vhs binary record_demo(), vhsr_check() gate path resolution (vhsr_vhs_path() etc.). Anything can express tape syntax, function can run. example produces:
code: vhsr_run_tape("scripts/my-demo.tape") vhsr_run_tape(' Output "demo.gif" Set Shell "bash" Set FontSize 22 Type "echo Hello from a hand-written tape!" Enter Sleep 800ms Type `ls -1 *.R | head -3` Enter Sleep 1s ')

"auto" (default) prefers "arf" (Rust-based modern R console tree-sitter syntax highlighting zero runtime dependencies — see https://github.com/eitsupi/arf), falls back "radian" found, otherwise plain "R". start_pause Delay R startup first typed line (e.g. "800ms"). end_pause Delay last typed line (hidden) q() exit (e.g. "500ms"). paragraph_pause set, blank lines expr produce sleep duration instead typed. typing_speed_jitter Numeric [0, 1]; positive, typed line uses speed sampled uniformly within ±jitter typing_speed. Set base::set.seed() calling reproducible jitter. tape Optional. raw .tape script string (path .tape file). supplied, expr styling args ignored tape run verbatim. quiet TRUE, suppress vhs stdout/stderr.
